newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC sees lower first half profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC sees lower first half profit.

text.p: Mining house WMC Ltd said on Friday that it expected earnings in the first half of the current year would be substantially lower than the year ago result.
The company also told shareholders at the annual general meeting that subdued conditions in terms of demand and prices which existed in the second half of 1995/96 had continued into the current year.
It said the full year result may be adversely affected by the continuing strength of the Australian dollar and lower metal prices if they persist.
Chairman Sir Arvi Parbo said the company has taken action to reduce costs in an attempt to counter lower prices and higher exchange rates, which were both beyond WMC's control.

"This will counter some of the negative effects but it is obvious that, should the lower prices and the higher exchange rate persist for the rest of the current financial year, the financial result for 1996/97 will be affected adversely," Parbo said.
"The profit for the first half will be substantially lower than for the first half of last year," he said.
Parbo said record production of nickel, alumina, and copper helped WMC achieve a 31.5 percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$392 million.
"In the second half of the year, markets weakened and at the end of the year the prices for our products were well below the average for 1995/96," he said.
"These subdued conditions have persisted since then."
Parbo said it was difficult to judge how long these poor conditions would persist, noting high economic growth in most Asian countries and modest growth in major world economies.
"There are some indications that the downturn may have bottomed, and some observers are predicting an improvement in the demand for metals and minerals in 1997," Parbo said.
"Time will tell whether they are right," he said.
WMC is one of the world's largest nickel producers from its operations in Western Australia, where it also has substantial gold mining interests.
The company produces uranium from the Olympic Dam mine in South Australia.
